newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen off $0.50-$1.00-trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen off $0.50-$1.00-trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen falling $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt amid increased hog marketings and retreating packer demand, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Top prices in Iowa and Minnesota were expected down $0.50 and seen ranging from $59.00 to $59.50 for hogs delivered to plants.
Illinois buyers said they expect hogs Wednesday to trade down $0.50 to $1.00, with a top of $57.50 to $58.00/plants.
Indiana buyers also look for $0.50 to $1.00 lower prices, with a possible top of $57.00 at plants.
Interior hog marketings Tuesday reportedly exceeded USDA estimates of 95,000 head as producers started selling hogs in an attempt to take advantage of Monday's higher prices.
Some of the increased marketings were attributed to producers trying to get current before the upcoming Labor Day holiday weekend.
Cash hog price weakness was furthered by talk that a major pork processor was starting to cut back operating hours in an attempt to reduce a backlog of loins, sources said.
